t.en: In this level the start is no longer filled in. The board holds the circuit you wired in <level-ref to="confluence"></level-ref>. When the robot reaches the start, up and left are both “out”, so the Merger receives nothing and can only output “—”, and every crossing after it reads nothing but “—”.

Under the view there is a This cell panel. Its “is start” is “yes” only while the robot stands on the start, and “no” on every other cell. Click it, and the This cell part on the left of the circuit board gains an output sending a yes / no signal: a diamond dot and a dashed wire.

Two new components: a <part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref> always outputs the same number; a <part-ref to="part:pass"></part-ref> lets its number through only when its condition port receives “yes”, and otherwise outputs “—”.

goal.en: Only right or down, and the start is no longer filled in. Have the robot write 1 on the start and up + left on every other crossing, so it counts the routes correctly in all three cities.

how.en: Click “is start” in the inputs window: the This cell part gets an output for it. If a test fails, the robot stops on the cell where it went wrong, and the numbers in the view and on the board are what it saw and computed there.

body.en: A Pass gate is like a door: on the start it opens and a 1 goes into the Merger; on any other cell it stays shut, and the Merger adds only up and left.
It got all three cities right: 3×4, 4×4 and 5×6. Give it a 100×100 city and the same board works just as well.
Every cell’s answer is computed from the answers of earlier cells and then recorded in the table. This method has a proper name: dynamic programming.

note.en: Wire the rule into a circuit and the machine can fill a table of any size. That is dynamic programming.

say.en: Step 1: click “is start” under This cell.
Step 2: drag a <part-ref to="part:const"></part-ref> and a <part-ref to="part:pass"></part-ref> from the tray onto the board.
The robot walks from the top left to the bottom right, so when it reaches a cell, the cells to its right and below are still empty and can’t be read.
With the Constant wired straight into the Merger, every crossing gets an extra 1. Use a Pass gate so it only goes through at the start.

hints.en: What should the start hold? That number must appear only on the start, while every other crossing stays up + left.
Wire “is start” into a Pass gate’s “if” port and a Constant 1 into its “num” port, then wire the Pass gate into the Merger’s free dot.
